summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and constipation lasting over a week. She had no active gastrointestinal bleeding, but her symptoms were likely exacerbated by severe constipation. Imaging revealed volume overload with bilateral pleural effusions and subcutaneous edema, consistent with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure. Her hypertension was managed with re-initiation of home medications, and her blood pressure stabilized. A urinary tract infection was suspected due to elevated white count and positive urinalysis; treatment was adjusted after urine culture showed yeast colonization. An aggressive bowel regimen resolved constipation, and she remained nausea-free after admission. Her renal function improved slightly, and electrolyte imbalances from diuresis were corrected. She was discharged back to extended care with medication adjustments, including increased metolazone and addition of Bisacodyl, and plans to address depression through rehab services.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
